text: The building you're in just came down on top of you.
Bricks and beams pin your legs to the floor and you can't move.
Rescuers dig by hand because one wrong move can bring more of it down.
They use dogs and drones and flashlights to find you.
But here's the scary part. Lifting the weight off can be the most dangerous moment.
Under all that weight the muscles in your legs start to break down.
Potassium leaks out of them and gets trapped there.
When the weight comes off it all rushes to your heart at once.
Too much potassium can make your heart beat wrong or even stop. It's called crush syndrome.
So rescuers try to get fluids into you before they lift the weight.
On November eleventh a three story building in Brooklyn fell into a deep hole being dug next door.
At least one person died and firefighters dug by flashlight into the night.
Subscribe because that's what really happens when a building falls on you.
